answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each new seat to inherit a vine of countersignatures from already-established miners, not from freshly minted keys. A sockpuppet farm parked on a digital tundra of unused addresses cannot grow that vine alone: each signer must first lock a stake and publish a cipher bound to a unique epoch seed as an admission proof, then wait for independent attestors to confirm the bond. Because both the stake and the peer-web are scarce, cheap clones fail to buy panel influence.
